title: Nasal [ɑ̃] — an, am, en, em (set 2)
focus: These spellings all make the nasal vowel [ɑ̃], as in « enfant ». In Québec it is usually pronounced further forward in the mouth than in Paris, so it can sound close to a Parisian « in » — listen for that. Careful: the verb ending -ent (« ils chantent ») is silent, never nasal, and a following vowel or doubled n/m cancels the nasal (« banane », « Jeanne »). « Jeanne » has a double n, so it isn't nasal.

sentences.en: My big sister is called Jeanne.

sentences.fr: Mon petit frère pose c[en]t questions par jour !
sentences.en: My little brother asks a hundred questions a day!

sentences.fr: Le dim[an]che, nous m[an]geons chez ma gr[an]d-mère.
sentences.en: On Sundays, we eat at my grandmother's.

sentences.fr: Elle prépare toujours un excell[en]t gâteau.
sentences.en: She always makes an excellent cake.
